claim: The wage Gini coefficient for US independent artists, writers and performers is 0.582 against a national average of 0.474, making earnings inequality inside this creator-adjacent occupation materially higher than in the US economy as a whole.
stance_target: The position that creative and creator occupations concentrate income far more unequally than ordinary labour markets, so median-and-mean reporting is mandatory
scope_conditions: United States only; Data USA visualisation of US Census ACS PUMS, 2024 reference year; NAICS industry group 'Independent artists, writers, and performers'; a third-party rendering of federal microdata rather than an official Census publication
quoted_support: Independent artists, writers, and performers has a wage GINI of 0.582, which is more than than the national average of 0.474.

claim: Full-time workers in the US independent-artists industry average $85,559 a year for 44.5 hours a week while part-time workers average $31,594 for 19.3 hours, a 2.7x annual gap on a 2.3x hours difference.
stance_target: The position that headline creative-occupation average earnings are carried by full-timers and that part-time creative work does not scale linearly to a living income
scope_conditions: United States only; ACS-derived, 2024 reference year; averages not medians, so upward-skewed
quoted_support: On average, full-time employees in the Independent artists, writers, and performers Industry Group work 44.5 hours per week and have an average annual salary of $85,559. Part-time employees in the same industry work 19.3 hours and earn an average annual salary of $31,594.

claim: The US independent-artists industry group records a self-identified workforce of 172,376 people in ACS data against only about 20,100 payroll employees in monthly BLS establishment data, an eightfold gap that is the self-employment share of the occupation.
stance_target: The position that establishment-based employment statistics cannot measure creator or independent-artist populations
scope_conditions: United States only; ACS workforce count for 2024 versus BLS monthly establishment employment as of February 2023; different reference dates, so the ratio is approximate; the two series measure different universes by design
quoted_support: As of February 2023, there are 20.1k people employed in the Independent Artists, Writers, and Performers industry. This represents a 11% increase in employment when compared to February 2022.

claim: BLS projects a 10-year employment decline of 1.61 percent for the US independent-artists industry alongside 27.2 percent projected output growth, implying output per worker rises while the number of people making a living this way does not.
stance_target: The position that creative-industry output growth does not translate into growth in the number of people who earn a living from it
scope_conditions: United States only; BLS employment projections as rendered by Data USA; 10-year horizon from a 2024 base; note the industry rate equals the stated national rate of -1.61 percent, which is anomalous and may be a rendering artefact of the source page
quoted_support: The national workforce is projected to grow -1.61% in the next ten years. The Independent Artists, Writers, and Performers industry has a lower projected workforce growth at -1.61%.
